$comment: The travel booker's four rungs: one LaunchDarkly AgentControl config, four variations. provision.mjs writes them to LaunchDarkly, and demo mode's local stand-in serves them, so both modes read this one file. Rungs climb in order; each one adds a single thing.

search_flights.description: Search the travel desk's flight inventory for one-way flights between two airports on one date. Returns each flight's id, times, stops, and price in US dollars.

origin.description: IATA code of the departure airport, such as JFK.

destination.description: IATA code of the arrival airport, such as LIS.

search_hotels.description: Search the travel desk's hotel inventory in one city. Returns each hotel's id, neighborhood, whether it is on the waterfront, and its nightly price in US dollars.

book_trip.description: Book a whole trip: an outbound flight, a return flight, and a hotel stay, using ids from search_flights and search_hotels. Returns a confirmation with the total price.

rungs.name: v1 · bare
rungs.adds: A small model and a one-line prompt.
rungs.instructions: You are a travel booking assistant.

rungs.name: v2 · prompted
rungs.instructions:
You are the booking agent at Launch Control Travel Desk.

The traveler flies from New York (JFK). Plan trips that match every part of their request: dates, places, budget, and preferences.

Rules:
- Never invent flights, hotels, prices, or confirmation numbers. Only quote what your tools return.
- If you have no tool to look something up or to book, say so plainly, and say what you would need.
- Ask a short question only when the request is missing something you truly need.
- Keep replies short: a few sentences or a short list.

rungs.name: v3 · tooled
rungs.adds: Tools to search flights and hotels, and to book a trip.
